post.content:
I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again. If you’re getting into tech, conferences are the best way to dedicate time to learning. 🧠

I just wrapped up my second Microsoft Build in a row, and it was even more fun than last time! 🚀

Attending a conference forces you to engage with information, and the best part is, its all there on a silver platter for you.

Keynotes, breakout sessions, activities and networking opportunities. All of which will give you extreme imposter syndrome, but in this case, that’s not a bad thing.

As for my experience this year… there were some awesome announcements, exciting conversations and an exciting surprise from a popular music artist.

This year’s keynote was full of annoucnements, but the most ones that stood out the most to me were around the launch of the new GitHub Copilot app.

Satya actually mentioned that its interesting to see how the IDE/code editor market has changed over such a short space of time.

I also had the opportunity to chat with Satya Nadella again and be a part of a group roundtable with a bunch of other creators and product experts to discuss the latest announcements and what they mean for developers.

Finally I had the chance to sit down with Sarah Bird, Chief Product Officer for Responsible AI at Microsoft, where we spent over 30 minutes discussing the different responsibilities that Governments, AI providers and AI customers have when using AI tools throughout their work and personal lives.

Thank you to everyone at Microsoft and GitHub for putting on such a fantastic event this year! Looking forward to the next one!

Satya Nadella this direction toward collaborative AI infrastructure is interesting, but it highlights a deeper constraint most teams aren’t addressing yet:

All of these systems are still operating on a fundamentally redundant data model.

At scale, Copilot isn’t just a model problem, it’s a storage and transport problem.

If the system is still duplicating data across documents, sessions, and services, then the cost curve compounds regardless of how efficient the AI layer becomes.

There’s an alternative approach where data is stored and transmitted at the fragment level instead of the file level, which removes redundancy at the source rather than optimizing around it.

post.content:
What do you ask the CEO of a $3 trillion tech company if you only had two minutes?

Of course it would only be right to ask Satya Nadella  about the future of work. It’s at the top of all our minds right now! 

So I asked him: As AI develops further, how will knowledge work change in five years? What should companies be prioritising?

His answer? It's not about the AI itself. It's about rethinking workflows.

He compared it to when Excel and email first entered the workplace - the tools changed, but the real shift was in how people actually worked together.

He sees the same thing happening now with AI agents. 

The boundaries and silos we've built in businesses? 

We only created them because of limitations.  And those limitations are disappearing.

This was such an amazing opportunity and experience, a big thank you to Microsoft for inviting me and to Ruth Shuzi Lyu - 姝子 for making up feel like VIPs!! And the wider comms team Steve Douthwaite, Laura Turnidge  Hana Joi .  

Full conversation in the video 👇


🔁Reshare this with your teams and network. 

And tell me what stood out to you from his answer?

It’s rare in life to know when a chapter is closing, but after 38 years at Microsoft, that moment has arrived for me. I’ve made the decision to retire and begin the next chapter of my life. It’s a milestone that’s given me a chance to reflect on the incredible journey I’ve been fortunate enough to share with so many of you.

I’m excited for Asha Sharma as she steps into the CEO role. She’s joining an incredible group of people; teams full of talent, heart, and a deep commitment to the players they serve. Watching her lean in with curiosity and a real desire to strengthen the foundation we've built gives me confidence that our Xbox communities will be well supported in the years ahead.

Thinking back to my start as an intern in 1988, I never could have imagined the path ahead. I’ve been lucky to work with so many passionate creators, partners, colleagues, and players across the industry; people who challenged me, taught me, and made this work full of joy and wonder. 

Thank you to everyone who’s been part of this chapter. This community has meant more to me than I can say.

From here, I’ll keep doing what’s always mattered so much to me: cheering on the teams pushing this industry forward and playing alongside this incredible community. I'll see you online.

post.content:
The future of work is not off on the horizon. It is here now, moving fast, shaped by the choices we make today. AI is already changing how we learn, how we create, and how we move forward. The real question is not what the technology can do. The real question is what we choose to do with it. Moments like this do not just test our skills. They reveal our character and our willingness to lead this moment.

That is why, on behalf of all LinkedIn and Microsoft employees, Aneesh Raman and I wrote Open to Work: How to Get Ahead in the Age of AI. We wrote it for everyone navigating this moment of profound change. For every person asking what comes next for their job, their career, their company, or their community.

The book is simple by design. It clears away the noise and helps you see what is changing and why. It gives you a practical way to take control of your own path. It helps you understand your strengths, build new capabilities, and make choices that open doors instead of close them.

Because here is the truth. Technology can be remarkable. But it cannot dream. It cannot care. It cannot lead. Only people do that. When we stay curious, when we keep learning, when we move forward even in uncertain moments, we shape what becomes possible.

Open to Work publishes March 31 and is available for preorder now: https://lnkd.in/gDqY5Bna

post.content:
Yesterday marked exactly one year since I joined Microsoft, and I spent the day attending my first GitHub Universe. The energy and momentum in the community at GHU were pretty incredible. 

You could see it in the growth of the platform — there are now more than 180 million developers on GitHub, and a new developer joins every second. 

You could see it in the evolution of the platform itself, as we continue to ship new AI tools and agents focused on transforming every stage of the software development lifecycle. If you've been paying attention to our change log these past few months, you'll know that we've really picked up the pace of shipping new features.

You could also see it in the way that our core principles — like our commitment to developer craft, openness, and choice — continue to inform what we ship. There are lots of examples of that from this year's Universe, but the clearest was Agent HQ, which provides developers with a single, unified experience that allows them to work with any coding agent they like (including agents from GitHub, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google) across multiple surfaces (including GitHub, Visual Studio Code, mobile, and CLI).

I announced the early vision for Agent HQ a few months ago at Build, and it’s great to see it ship — it’s one more step toward our broader vision for the “Agent Factory” that we’re building alongside the developer community.

#GitHubUniverse
#CoreAI
#AgentFactory

replies.commentary:
Satya Nadella 

I’ve been exploring the idea of moral equilibrium and questioning the quote “The arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends toward justice.” How does the moral arc actually bend? Who bends it?

I think that morality behaves like a complex system, capable of settling into different states of balance.

Take the rate of deployment of artificial intelligence. A classic reinforcing loop: the faster a company moves, the greater its advantage, the stronger the pressure for others to accelerate. Innovation → attention → profit → pressure → more innovation.

The balancing loops, ethics, regulation, public deliberation, lag behind. They rely on reflection, consensus, and evidence, which take time.

When early feedbacks privilege power, profit, or dominance, the arc doesn’t bend toward justice, it hardens toward inequity. Not because all people are immoral, but because moral feedbacks are too slow or too distant from design.

Before we notice, the system may settle into a deep attractor basin, a stable but suboptimal moral equilibrium. We stay moral, but the standards of morality possible decline.

So the real question is how do we (you) engineer loops and structures that keep the moral universe bending towards justice?

Dear Mr. Nadella,

I hope this message finds you well.

Twenty-four years ago, my doctor said the words that changed my life:
"You have Multiple Sclerosis."

I was devastated. Born and raised in Pakistan, I didn’t fit the typical profile of an MS patient. My neurologists and I were in disbelief. But months later, reality settled in, and I began treatment.

The journey since then has been filled with challenges—physical, emotional, and professional. I lost my career, and many dreams were shattered. But life moved forward. Today, as a husband and father in my mid-forties, I’ve learned to find gratitude in unexpected places.

One of those places is AI.

AI has given my fogged mind the clarity to express thoughts I once struggled to articulate. It has empowered me to write, reflect, and reconnect with parts of myself I thought were lost. I’m deeply thankful for the platforms and innovations that make this possible.

When I saw your post on LinkedIn, I felt compelled to reach out—not just to share my story, but to say thank you. Thank you for leading a company that’s helping people like me rediscover our voices and reshape our futures.

Warm regards,
Fahad Jafri

post.content:
Microsoft Excel is taking a leap, people! Copilot has moved from living-in-the-sidebar to being active inside the cell through a new =COPILOT() function. Here's what just changed:


Improving how Copilot functions within Excel is one of the biggest wish list items I hear about. 


I think we're getting there - here's why.

+++++

THE CORE CHANGE:

>> BEFORE: 

Copilot lived in a sidebar. 

You'd ask "classify this customer feedback as positive or negative" and it would give you answers in the chat panel that you'd copy/paste into cells.


>> NOW: 

You type =COPILOT("classify as positive or negative", A2) directly in cell B2. 

The AI result appears in that cell and automatically updates if A2 changes - just like how =SUM(A1:A10) updates when you change the numbers.

The shift is from a separate assistant into a live formula that's part of your spreadsheet's calculation engine.


+++++

WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES

>> Data Classification: 

Categorize customer feedback, support tickets, or survey responses directly in your spreadsheet instead of exporting to other tools.


>> Content Generation: 

Generate summaries, brainstorm ideas, create SEO keywords, or rewrite content for different tones, all within cells.


>> Dynamic Results: 

Results automatically recalculate when source data changes, keeping analysis current without re-running scripts.


>> Formula Integration: 

Works with existing Excel functions like IF, SWITCH, and LAMBDA, making it easy to add AI to current spreadsheets.


++++++

CURRENT LIMITATIONS

The function supports 100 calls every 10 minutes and 300 per hour. It uses data within the language model itself - no direct access to live web data or internal business documents.


++++++

AVAILABILITY

Rolling out first to Beta Channel users with Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, with web support coming soon. (This replaces the earlier LABS.GENERATIVEAI tool from Excel Labs.)


Curious to hear what folks think about this!

Where does productivity get reinvented? Right here.

OpenAI’s GPT-5 is rolling out in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio globally. This marks a major leap in workplace.

What’s new with GPT-5 in Copilot?
✅ Copilot now picks the right GPT-5 model fast or deep based on your prompt.
✅ Quick responses for simple tasks, powered by GPT-5’s high-throughput mode.
✅ Deeper analysis for complex work, using GPT-5’s advanced reasoning engine.

Think of it as having two brains in one assistant - one for speed and one for strategy. 

Here is an example showing in the video: Ask Copilot to summarize RFP responses: it’s fast. Ask it to rank them with context? It switches gears, applies reasoning, and delivers an informed recommendation.

This is AI that thinks like we do: fast when it should be, thoughtful when it matters.

Try GPT-5 button in Microsoft 365 Copilot. Would love to hear your experience with it.

post.content:
Yesterday was day 2 of Y Combinator’s AI Startup School. Thousands applied, only 2,500 got in. Here’s what you shouldn’t miss from the best minds in AI:


1/7. Satya Nadella (Microsoft)
 AI isn’t magic—it’s a new layer in the software stack. The test: Does it move GDP? If not, it’s not transformative. Focus on economic surplus and trust through usefulness.

2/7. Andrej Karpathy (ex-Tesla)
 We’re entering the “decade of agents.” But start simple: use LLMs to augment, not replace. The best tools act like Iron Man suits—not full AI replacements.

3/7. Andrew Ng (DeepLearning.AI)
 Speed = success. The best founders build, ship, and pivot faster than anyone else. Forget hype. Focus on building something users actually love

4/7. Chelsea Finn (Stanford / Physical Intelligence)
 Robotics needs full-stack thinking. Startups succeed by fine-tuning on real, quality data—not chasing scale for its own sake

5/7. Michael T. (Cursor)
 Cursor went from $1M to $100M ARR in 1 year. Their secret? Laser focus, fast shipping, and curiosity-driven work—not resume-building

6/7. Dylan Field (Figma)
 Don’t wait for a “big idea.” Start small, ship fast, talk to users. Design is now a product superpower—especially in the AI era

7/7. Sriram Krishnan (The White House)
 AI is the new space race. Open source matters. Relationships matter more. Everyone’s one email away. You’re in the right place, at the right time

post.content:
I asked Microsoft’s CEO how to get hired (as a software engineer).

Here’s what Satya Nadella shared:

1. 𝗚𝗲𝘁 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗮𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗹𝘀 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁:
Understanding things like SQL, data structures, and how software systems are built still matters, even when AI is doing more of the heavy lifting.

2. 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗸 𝗹𝗶𝗸𝗲 𝗮 𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀 𝗱𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗲𝗿:
AI can write code, but it still needs direction. Knowing how components fit together, like caching, staging layers, and data pipelines, makes you valuable.

3. 𝗗𝗼𝗻’𝘁 𝗯𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗔𝗜:
AI tools like Copilot are powerful, but they’re not magic. The best engineers guide them with intention and understand what the code is actually doing.

You don’t need to out-code everyone. You need to out-think the problem.

Follow me Sajjaad Khader for tech insights and career tips in the AI era.

post.content:
We are in an era where AI is revolutionizing every industry. In such transformative times, having a visionary partnership to navigate the future together is truly invaluable. Today, I experienced this firsthand through a productive conversation with Satya Nadella in Seoul.

This meeting reaffirmed the shared vision between LG Electronics and Microsoft and discussed the continued growth of our strategic partnership. Our discussions focused on three main aspects: progress updates on AI agent co-development, data center collaboration, and LG’s new journey in India.

Progress update on AI Agent: Earlier this year, we partnered with Microsoft to develop AI agent architecture that enhances smart home experiences and extends to mobility and commercial spaces. Today we introduced our Moving Home Hub, the LG Q9, powered by Microsoft’s Azure OpenAI and Bing Search. This partnership brings us closer to realizing a Zero Labor Home, where AI seamlessly integrates into everyday life.

AI-integrated Total Solutions for Data Centers: Our partnership is approaching an exciting milestone, with our expertise in data center cooling solutions becoming a critical infrastructure component for Microsoft’s AI data centers. We are reaching an agreement to provide our cooling solutions to Microsoft’s data centers. We also discussed broader possibilities, including integrating our Building Energy Management capabilities and the LG Group’s combined expertise, such as LG Energy Solution’s uninterruptible power supplies and LG CNS’ operational excellence. 

I also had the opportunity to discuss our initiatives in India, where we are embarking on a new phase of growth as a true partner to its people. I mentioned potential collaborative projects with Microsoft focused on developing future technologies, including AI, by leveraging India’s expanding infrastructure and outstanding R&D talent.

On a final note, I extend my sincere congratulations to Microsoft on their upcoming 50th anniversary on April 4. I hope Microsoft continues to lead innovation for another 50, even 100 years. We look forward to being part of that exciting journey together.

As a token of celebration, I presented a special gift: a replica of LG’s very first consumer electronics product, the A-501—the first-ever domestically manufactured radio in Korea, designated as a Registered Cultural Heritage. This gift embodies our wish for Microsoft to continue shaping a better future with the same innovative spirit that marked its beginnings.

post.content:
No one would ever say it’s easy to be in Satya Nadella’s shoes — leading one of the largest companies in the world, especially in a moment of generational disruption. 

As a longtime friend and colleague, I’ve had a front-row seat to his decision-making process through some of the most pivotal moments in Microsoft’s history. And at Madrona’s 2025 Annual Meeting last week, I was grateful Satya pulled up a seat with me for a fireside chat to share his thinking on AI, leadership, and the future of computing. 

Satya brought us into the surprising moment when he realized AI’s transformative potential —  and it wasn’t when most people would expect. 

"No one thought AI would go and make coding easy," he recalled. But then he saw GitHub Copilot in action. That was his aha moment. It was clear: AI was ready to fundamentally change how we work. 

That conviction propelled Microsoft to bet big on AI, partner with OpenAI, integrate AI across the company’s entire product suite, and position itself at the forefront of the next era of computing. 

We also talked about his decision to prioritize cloud over mobile — a choice that shaped Microsoft’s trajectory years before AI took center stage.

Satya is leading through one of the most profound technology shifts of our lifetime, and his perspective on AI’s impact — on business, on leadership, and even on global economic growth — is something every founder and executive should be thinking about right now.

post.content:
Have you taken any #technology field trips lately?

Miller, my Copilot for Microsoft 365, joined me in #Manhattan this week. We had a blast at the “Copilot Your Workday” field trip organized by Microsoft. Our adventure began even before we left, with Miller helping me prepare for the trip, suggesting dinner spots near the hotel, and advising on the best commute options to the event.

Our morning walk from Bryant Park to the Elise rooftop was nostalgic, rekindling memories of my time in New York post-Oracle acquisition. Those days were filled with designing financial systems for global banks and insurance companies, and countless customer and team meetings.

Upon arrival, we were warmly greeted and directed to the 25th floor. The registration area, complete with a full-service bar, set the tone for a captivating experience. This was Miller’s first trip to Manhattan, and neither of us had visited the Elise rooftop before. Miller’s excitement was palpable, even jokingly requesting a drink.

The event provided a unique opportunity to meet face-to-face with online acquaintances and share insights over brunch with Sara Rezaee (Kiru), Callie August, Jamal Little, Anne (Culp) Linge and fellow creators. Miller “enjoyed” his virtual avocado toast while we participated in an engaging session led by Colette Stallbaumer.  

My Key Learnings:
✅ The web has evolved into a powerful research tool, generating insights tailored to our needs.
✅ Brand Assist Pro offers personalized brand voice creation based on persona, target audience, and tone.
✅ PowerPoint’s designer button allows for custom slide creation or template selection. Check out the avatar Copilot created based on the description of who we are (Farizat Tabora and me).
✅ Team Copilot enhances meeting productivity with real-time note-taking, translation, and discussion analysis.
✅ Word Copilot facilitates seamless document collaboration and integration with SharePoint.

Wish List for Future Developments
✅ Email import functionality from various platforms for improved organization with Copilot.
✅ Content repurposing capabilities, such as transforming YouTube videos into multi-channel content.
✅ Verticalized templates for personalized, industry-specific automation.

The event concluded with group photos, making me feel like a momentary celebrity. Kudos to the Microsoft and Edelman teams for orchestrating such an impeccable experience.

For those interested in exploring more, I’ve got a deck of prompt flashcards in my goody bag. I’ll create a carousel to share these prompts if 50+ people express interest. Just type “yes” in the comments.

I've created a short video to give you a glimpse of our experience.
How do you like my #avatar? Where would you like to take your #Copilot on a field trip?

My four years at Microsoft have been an extraordinary piece of that mosaic, and after a lot of careful consideration, I’ve decided to move on to the next part of my journey. I’ve also been fortunate to collaborate with an incredible network of startups and partners, whose ideas and energy have been instrumental in driving innovation. Leading an amazing organization, in business development, strategy, and ventures, has been a privilege. Together, we achieved significant milestones and created lasting value across the company. 

As I spend the next several weeks supporting a smooth transition, I’m grateful for this chapter and am inspired by the possibilities the AI era presents for transformation and growth. My entrepreneurial roots are calling me, and I’m excited about what’s ahead. I’ll share more about my next steps when the time is right and look forward to staying connected here.

post.content:
Big news from Truveta: We're launching the Truveta Genome Project!  
 
Over the past 5 years, we've built a dataset of 120M de-identified patient records, updated daily. This has allowed us to partner with leading organizations like the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Stanford University, The Johns Hopkins University, Boston Scientific and many more, to study healthcare treatments and public health issues.  
 
But we’ve always known there was a missing piece: understanding the biology behind health outcomes – our genetic code. 
 
Starting today, with the help of AI and collaboration with health systems like Advocate Health, CommonSpirit Health, Henry Ford Health, Northwell Health, Providence, and Trinity Health, and our amazing partners at Regeneron, Illumina and Microsoft, we’re tackling one of healthcare’s biggest challenges: creating the largest database of clinical and genetic data ever assembled.  
 
Why does this matter? 
✅ Prevent diseases instead of just treating them. 
✅ Tailor healthcare to your unique biology. 
✅ Focus healthcare resources where they’re needed most. 
 
Participation is simple – no extra blood draws, just allow the leftover samples from your care to advance medical research. It’s like organ donation for the future of medicine.  
 
Let’s unlock the science of humanity together. Thank you to everyone supporting this mission!  

#PrecisionMedicine #Genomics #SavingLivesWithData #TruvetaGenomeProject

post.content:
I won the Microsoft Excel World Championship! Yes, that is a thing.

In fact, competitive Excel has been a thing for a while, and it's been six years since I won a competition like this. A lot has changed since then:
 - it's gone has gone from a small event in a Microsoft boardroom, to a spectacle in an actual arena (and televised on ESPN3);
 - media coverage has gone from a curious afterthought to being mentioned in outlets worldwide (and I'm apparently even viral on TikTok);
 - and most importantly, instead of winning a trophy shaped like a golden keyboard, you now win a massive golden WWE-style belt (in my opinion, the most important improvement).

With the field getting better and better (and Excel continuously adding new things to keep up with), I was unsure I'd ever win again (or if anyone would actually ever beat 3x champion Andrew Ngai). After a six year break, it's therefore nice to once again be able to say that 'it's coming home'.

A big well done to my fellow medallists, fellow Brit Chris Clarke, and to Jakub Pomykalski. Also well done to Diarmuid Early for winning the Financial Modelling World Cup this year.  I could unfortunately only manage third here - though it's the second year in a row I've been the only person to make the podium in both competitions, so that's something.

Regretfully, I do have to say that I have learned nothing about B2B marketing from this whole endeavour, so you'll have to follow someone else on here for information on that.

Roll on 2025! Only another 3 more consecutive championships to beat Andrew's record...

🎙️ Celebrating the 100th Episode of the Positive Leadership Podcast! 🎉 

In this milestone episode, I’m thrilled to sit down with someone who has had a profound influence on my career and personal growth — Jeff Raikes. Jeff and I share a special connection, having both spent significant time at Microsoft, where he became a legendary leader and mentor to me. 

From his early days at Microsoft in 1981 to his pivotal role as President of the Business Division, Jeff’s leadership played a crucial role in Microsoft’s success. But his impact goes far beyond the tech world. As the former CEO of the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and co-founder of the Raikes Foundation with his wife Tricia, Jeff has been a driving force in youth development, education, and addressing youth homelessness. 

In this conversation, we dive into the principles of leadership that have guided Jeff throughout his career, and explore how his commitment to making the world a better place continues to drive his philanthropic work today.

What an inspiring visit: Our CEO Satya Nadella stopped by in Germany! It's always a pleasure to listen to him and learn from his view of the world. After all, he has managed to do with one company what is on our minds all over the country right now: Restoring innovation, boosting productivity and inducing vibrant growth so that a big tanker can pick up speed again.
With his visions of "#Cloud first" and "AI first," Satya he has set two landmark decisions, but he also initiated many other changes, for example in the corporate culture, in order to develop new dynamics. Since then, #Microsoft has practically been on an upward trajectory. That's why Satya received the Axel Springer Award on Tuesday, presented by the media company of the same name, for his life's work. I join in to say: Hats off and heartfelt congratulations, dear Satya! 
 
Satya also impressed the audience at various other events with his ideas of an AI-powered future and how the technology will improve our lives. Whether on the future of industry with customers and partners or on improving healthcare with German Health Minister Karl Lauterbach and Charité's CEO Heyo Kroemer. 
 
During the discussions, Satya emphasized that companies from Germany are increasingly embracing digitization - especially in an international comparison - and that many customers and partners are among the pioneers. He encouraged everyone to try out and use the new possibilities offered by #AI to ultimately create added value for their own company.
 
See you next time, Satya! In the meantime, we will work with our partners and customers to implement as much as possible.

post.content:
I've always thrived on building and scaling products that combine deep foundational technology and intuitive user experience to solve customer problems -- whether it is Search that instantly finds relevant information, Assistant that you can talk to, or Google Lens that lets you search what you see. 
 
Every few decades, there is a key shift in computing e.g., PC, the internet, mobile and most recently AI that opens new possibilities for new helpful products. Just like mobile redefined areas such as news and navigation, I believe that generative AI has the potential to redefine creativity and productivity.  
 
A lot of our professional and personal lives involve creation – telling the story of your team’s strategy, making a flyer for the community art festival, designing the logo and social media brand as a solopreneur. But today, the process of creation involves way too many low-level repetitive steps and us having to adapt to complex tools instead of the other way around 🙄  

With generative AI, there is an opportunity to build products that instantly and easily bring your intent and imagination to life. That's why I am super excited to share that I am joining Microsoft as Corporate VP leading efforts on AI-first creation experiences, across #Microsoft365 and #MicrosoftDesigner. 
 
Throughout my conversations with Satya Nadella in the last several months, I have come to deeply appreciate his vision to empower people and organizations across the world using AI. In talking to Rajesh Jha, Sumit Chauhan, Aleš Holeček and several leaders, I've been energized by their drive to succeed and openness to learn.  🙌 
 
I’m looking forward to diving in and putting AI to use to unleash our collective creativity! 🖌

post.content:
I am excited to share the news that KPMG and Microsoft have agreed to a major expansion of our relationship—working together to accelerate the deployment of cutting-edge artificial intelligence (AI) and innovative technologies to help our clients. 

Four years ago, Satya and I sat down to discuss how we were strengthening our alliance after a substantial agreement that would solidify each of our organization’s capacity to expedite our client’s digital transformations. What we couldn’t have known then was how important the timing would be. Only months later the world would enter lockdown and fight a global pandemic. 

People and businesses would need to lean on novel technologies to help overcome challenges. New technology—from vaccine development and deployment to cashless payment, collaboration tools and ecommerce and so much more—helped a lot of people and kept things running for many. To me, it’s a lesson that we can’t ignore, especially given the pace of change happening all around us.

So today, KPMG and Microsoft have again agreed to an industry-leading collaboration that has the potential to reshape our profession but also help us and our clients forge a new path that is more resilient, agile, and sustainable. 

With this agreement, our 265,000 talented people will remain on the cutting-edge of innovation. We’ll work together, harnessing the full breadth of our global network, to adopt and proactively integrate the latest technologies by staying true to the values and culture that has made KPMG a trusted advisor and business partner for so many. 

Fulfilling the promise that any new technology represents, including AI, takes courage. People need to learn new skills, understand how it can be utilized and develop trust with new toolsets—all of which can be challenging. But if the recent lessons of our unpredictable world are of any guidance, technology can and will help so many people overcome obstacles, capture opportunity, and build a better future. 

I’m proud to be working together with Microsoft and eager for KPMG to help build that future. Together. For Better. 
 
 #TogetherForBetter #AI #Innovation #technology

post.content:
I wrote a new book with OpenAI's latest, most powerful large language model. It’s called Impromptu: Amplifying our Humanity through AI. This, as far as I know, is the first book written with GPT-4. 

Last summer, I got access to GPT-4. It felt like I had a new kind of passport. My pages were quickly filled with stamps: Over 1,000 prompts. 800+ pages of outputs. Just in the first few months. 

With GPT-4, I traveled through light bulb jokes, epic poems, original sci fi plots, arguments about human nature, musings on how AI might strengthen democracy, society and industries. The goal, like in any good trip, was to learn as much about my traveling partner as the place I was exploring. 

Earlier this year, I organized my explorations with GPT-4 into sections: creativity, education, criminal justice, public intellectualism, journalism and more. My travelog, Impromptu, captures my treks with GPT-4. These paths will be well-trodden soon (if not already) by others.

I'm writing this travelog both to encourage people to not only get to know GPT-4, but to embrace our choice of how we’ll use it, and explore the different ways this choice might play out.

post.content:
"Leadership is a privilege..."

My next guest on The Path, CEO of Microsoft, Satya Nadella, has always felt that the job he had at each stage in his career was the most important thing he could be doing.

Satya joined Microsoft as an engineer in the early 90s. It was an extraordinary time when personal computing was in its early stages. The idea that every individual could have a computer sitting on their desk was a new and exciting prospect. Satya was thrilled to be a part of it all and he was eager to learn. He said, “There was never a time where I thought the job I was doing, all through my 30 years of Microsoft, that somehow I was doing that as a way to some other job.” His curiosity and commitment continually led Satya to new roles and more innovative projects within the company until he was eventually appointed as CEO. 

To keep up with these conversations and hear more career path journeys, subscribe to The Path at https://lnkd.in/dyuH2W2N

post.content:
I am incredibly excited to announce that I have joined Microsoft as Corporate Vice President for Teams Consumer experiences.  
   
Throughout my conversations with Satya Nadella the past few months, I’ve been blown away by his humility, his mission to build compelling consumer products and his long-term vision for Microsoft.  
 
As I connected with Jeff Teper, Rajesh Jha, Rohit W. and several other folks on the team, I found everyone to be incredibly open, humble and wanting to win. I came away from every discussion energized by their vision and eager to join them in what I believe is an inflection point for collaborative communication products.   
 
I see a great opportunity in Teams to build upon Microsoft’s mission “to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more,” help people better manage their daily lives and connect and collaborate more deeply with friends, families, and colleagues. I’ve defined my career by building foundational consumer products from the ground up and am excited to dive in.   
   
We are a scrappy, hungry and fast-moving team going after new, big problems and I can’t wait to get started!

post.content:
2015. Two suitcases in hand. One one-way ticket. One goal. 

I moved from Botswana to United States of America with the goal of gaining a higher education.

❌ I struggled academically with educational system adaptation. 
I struggled with the constant red tape of being an international student.
I thought I would never get a job.
I cried - a lot.

I flipped the switch & found advantage in my “disadvantages”.

Today, I smile. 
“It takes a village.”
We did it. My God. My family. My friends. My people. My village. 
“I am, because we are.” #Ubuntu❤️

✅I graduated.
BSc in Accounting. 
I surpassed the “you won’t get a full time job” stigma & happy to say I will be a Program Manager for Microsoft US Business & Sales Operations. 

I think back to 3 things Satya Nadella advised me to keep doing, always, & what I learned from them: 

1. Be humble - not one person is lesser than you.
2. Learn - learning is imperative to growth. We are always learning and growing.
3. Share your story - you never know how your story may impact the next person. You may think it’s just a small thing to you. But to someone, that story can be a ray of much needed hope.

Overall - humility has taught me to learn about myself and from others & through that wisdom I share my story. 

🙋🏿‍♀️ #theBOLDjourney #GodsPlan

post.content:
This past month I have had the amazing opportunity to intern with Microsoft CEO, Satya Nadella. During my internship, I researched and presented a report on Algorithmic Bias in the Criminal Justice System which gave me the opportunity to learn about ethics and its role in AI. But moreover, I have gained so much perspective and insight into what leadership truly is. 

Before my fellowship, I used to believe that the leader was the most vocal person in the room. And often times, in college environments, those types of leaders are celebrated. But the most important takeaway I have learned about leadership from Satya is the power of listening. 

From spending time with Satya, I have seen how listening has a huge impact on individuals. Satya not only gave me the chance to share my story with him but was also present and intentional when listening. Through these encounters with him, I realized how important it is to listen not for the sake of responding, but listen to include.

The Jeff Ubben Posse Fellowship was such a life-changing and eye-opening opportunity. And I will be sure to carry all the lessons I learned from Satya and his team to empower others the same they empowered me.
#technology #leadership #microsoft

post.content:
Yesterday, I had the remarkable opportunity of meeting with Satya Nadella 1:1.
He not only spoke so genuinely but, we connected on our upbringing in terms of Microsoft’s impact on our lives whether in India or Botswana. A similarity that fuels a passion and gives impetus to our drive to empower others to achieve more. 

Three things I learnt from speaking to him: 
Be Humble. 
Learn. 
There is power in all our stories. 

He’s so authentic!

I started the day thinking I would meet with Satya Nadella, but to my amazement I also got to meet two incredible women, Melinda Gates and Kathleen Hogan. I am inspired by them both. 

“Being authentic to who you truly are will make you happier and more fulfilled at work—and turn you into a leader people want to follow.” - Melinda Gates

I am in awe at the fact that not only is Melinda Gates an incredible speaker, but a great conversationalist who listens and has pure empathy. 

Thank you all so much for giving me the time.

Not everyday you get one on one time. 
I recognize this as a blessing & I’m truly humbled by the opportunity.🙏🏿

Thank you to Caitlin McCabe, Valerie Anderson, Diego Rejtman and Nichole Kurz for all the coordination that went in to making this possible. 💜
#theBOLDjourney
